components.value:
The title doctor honoris causa is an honorary academic title awarded to outstanding personalities for their contributions to a specific field of science, culture, art, etc., serving as recognition of their lifelong work. It entitles the holder to use the abbreviation Dr. h. c. after their name.

TBU has so far awarded 5 honorary doctorates. For an institution open to global trends, it is certainly not surprising that all recipients of this rank from Zlín University are figures with international reach.

components.title: TBU Honorary Doctorate Recipients
components.value: The first recipient of the honorary doctorate was the President of the European Commission, José Manuel Barroso. Practically immediately after the Czech Republic entered the European Union, TBU took the step of recognizing this fact with a formal academic act. This was finally accomplished on April 22, 2009, when José Manuel Barroso, then President of the European Commission, received the honorary doctorate during a ceremony in the newly constructed University Center. 'I am convinced that the award of the honorary doctorate is proof that you hold the European idea dear. In Europe... we will need young people who are capable of thinking critically and who have a strong sense of values. I know that this university is very careful to ensure its students identify with strong ethical principles,' said the awardee in his speech.

slides.description: The fifth prestigious title of honoris causa in sequence was received on March 5, 2025, in the assembly hall of Zlín University by Prof. Vladimír Kučera. His research in the analysis and synthesis of control circuits influenced entire generations of scientists and engineers. He is an extraordinary scientist and educator of international caliber who has won many prestigious awards during his career. The award of the honorary title Dr. h. c. by the Zlín university was thus not only a worthy recognition of his work, but also another confirmation of his exceptional position in the global scientific community.

components.value:
Two years later, on May 18, 2011, the second TBU honorary doctorate was received by a lady whose name is known (not only) by architects all over the world: Prof. Eva Jiřičná. This Zlín native, during decades of work in the field of architecture and design, has left traces in New York, London, Moscow, Dubai, Prague – as well as in her hometown. And it was precisely for her life's work, for her excellent presentation of TBU in the Czech Republic and abroad, and for spreading the good name of the university and the city of Zlín that she was honored by the university. 'It takes the effort of a whole team to complete even the smallest building... At the same time, it takes an even bigger team to bring humanity into our hearts,' Eva Jiřičná remarked during the ceremony.

The following year, on April 26, 2012, the university honored another lady whose name is known worldwide. The honorary doctorate was accepted by Sonja Baťa, wife of the former first Chairman of the TBU Board of Governors, Tomáš Baťa Jr. Through her, the university expressed its relationship with the entire Baťa family – as Mrs. Sonja herself emphasized: '... the award you are giving me, you are simultaneously giving to my husband, who brought me to Zlín. TBU mattered to him very much. He dreamed that the university would grow and become the intellectual center of his hometown.'

There are not many people in the Czech Republic who do not know the name of Ing. Miroslav Zikmund, one of the pair of famous Czech travelers of the 20th century who connected his life with Zlín. He became the 4th holder of the title doctor honoris causa of TBU on February 13, 2014.

'We decided to award Mr. Zikmund an honorary doctorate for his admirable life's work, which, together with his long-time colleague and friend Jiří Hanzelka, significantly enriched and expanded many areas of human knowledge,' explained then-rector Prof. Petr Sáha. The honorary doctorate was a 'birthday present' for Mr. Zikmund – the ceremony took place the day before his 95th birthday. 'It is an honor for TBU to award the title of honorary doctor to Miroslav Zikmund. With the courage with which he set off together with his friend to meet new knowledge and adventures, in his meticulous study and patient documentation of findings, but also in his firm human positions with which he faced adversity, he can be an example not only to students of Zlín university,' said Prof. Sáha during the presentation.

slides.description: The first recipient of the honorary doctorate of TBU in Zlín was the President of the European Commission, José Manuel Barroso. The honorary title Dr. h. c. was awarded to him for personal merit in joining the Czech Republic to the European Union and in building a new Europe. He received it at the University Center in Zlín on April 20, 2009, from the hands of the then-rector Prof. Ignác Hoza.

World-renowned architect, Prof. Eva Jiřičná, was awarded an honorary doctorate from our university on May 18, 2011. The university awarded her the title for her life's work, for her excellent presentation of the university and the city of Zlín in the Czech Republic and in the world, and for spreading the good name of the university and the city of Zlín. Pictured with the then vice-rector for international relations, Assoc. Prof. PhDr. Ing. Aleš Gregar, CSc.

On April 26, 2012, the university honored another lady whose name is known worldwide. The honorary doctorate was awarded to Sonja Baťa, wife of the former first Chairman of the TBU Board of Governors, for her long-term support and promotion of TBU abroad and for her personal contribution to the development of TBU's international relations.

The phenomenal traveler, writer, and publicist Ing. Miroslav Zikmund of the Hanzelka + Zikmund duo received an honorary doctorate just before his 95th birthday, on February 13, 2014. He thus became the fourth recipient of the honorary title doctor honoris causa of Zlín university. The title was awarded to him for his admirable life's work, which, together with his long-time colleague and friend Jiří Hanzelka, significantly enriched and expanded many areas of human knowledge.

The fifth prestigious title of honoris causa in sequence was received on March 5, 2025, in the assembly hall of Zlín University by Prof. Vladimír Kučera. His research in the analysis and synthesis of control circuits influenced entire generations of scientists and engineers. He is an extraordinary scientist and educator of international caliber who has won many prestigious awards during his career. The award of the honorary title Dr. h. c. by the Zlín university was thus not only a worthy recognition of his work, but also another confirmation of his exceptional position in the global scientific community.

components.title: Other interesting facts
components.value:
The fifth prestigious title of honoris causa in sequence was received on March 5, 2025 in the assembly hall of Zlín University by Prof. Vladimír Kučera. His research in the analysis and synthesis of control circuits influenced entire generations of scientists and engineers. During his career, Prof. Kučera has won many prestigious awards. He was the first Czech to be elected a Fellow of the prestigious IEEE institute. In 2021, he received the National Government Prize 'Česká hlava', which is the highest scientific award in the Czech Republic. He also became a member of the American Philosophical Society. Before him, only T. G. Masaryk, Edvard Beneš, and Václav Havel received this honor.

'In the case of Prof. Kučera, this is an extraordinary scientific and pedagogical figure of global dimensions. All the more our university values cooperation with him,' said Rector Prof. Milan Adámek at the ceremony.
